guide: Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: days between counts, count tolerance, shrink target, markup wanted, vehicle budget a day and the price rise to test on tools.
Check Technicians and Vans. They hold your people, vans and the lease cost a month that the other sheets look up.

List the parts you carry on each van on Van Stock with a minimum, a maximum and the quantity on hand. The below-minimum check, the quantity to reach the maximum and the restock cost fill in by themselves.

Count each van and write the expected and counted quantity on Stock Counts. The variance, the missing value and the recount flag calculate themselves; Shrink by Van adds up the stock missing between counts.
Write each restock on Restocks and each part used on a job on Parts Used with whether it left the van and whether it was billed. Unbilled Parts ranks what is still to bill.
Keep Parts, Supplier Price Changes and Price Book up to date. Price Change Margin Impact then shows the lines and open estimates that fell under your margin.
Enter the vehicle costs of each van every month on Vehicle Costs. Vehicle Cost by Van shows the cost per working day and per job against the shop and the service dates.
Log every tool and piece of equipment you buy on Tools and Equipment with its life in years. The Tool Replacement Plan shows the budget for each year.
Use the 18 tools: each answers one question with a verdict. Change the yellow inputs to try another van, category, season or price.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Parts and Van Dashboard and the Charts every week. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets with one row in Vans; a shop with several vans uses every row.

listing.title: HVAC and Plumbing Contractor Excel Template: Van Stock, Parts Used, Unbilled Parts, Price Changes, Vehicle Cost, Tool Budget
listing.headline: What is on every van, what it costs to run and which parts were never billed
listing.description:
Run the parts and vehicles of an HVAC and plumbing contractor business in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-run residential and light-commercial service shop with 1 to 15 technicians and a van for each lead technician. A one-person owner-operator with one van uses the same sheets with one row; a shop with several vans uses every row.

Van Stock holds every part on every van with a minimum, a maximum and the quantity on hand, and works out the parts below minimum, the quantity to reach the maximum and the cost of the next supplier run. Stock Counts compares expected with counted, and Shrink by Van adds up the stock missing between counts for each van and driver. Parts Used links every part to a job and shows which parts left a van and were never billed. Supplier Price Changes and the Price Book show which flat-price lines and open estimates fell under your margin after a supplier raised a cost, ranked by money at risk.

Vehicle Costs tracks fuel, repairs, tyres, lease and insurance by van and month, with the cost per working day and per job against the shop average and the service dates. Tools and Equipment logs every purchase with its life and builds a replacement budget for each year. 18 tools answer weekly questions with a clear verdict: restock list, count variance, shrink, stock turnover, short-stock vans, price change impact, markup check, unbilled parts, usage forecast, vehicle cost, keep or replace a van and stock-up before the season. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to technicians, apprentices, the office, your parts counter, your equipment supplier, the accountant and the insurance agent.

This is part five of the HVAC and Plumbing Contractor suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no per-technician fee: you keep your data. A demo copy full of sample data and a blank copy are included. It helps you keep track of your business and does not promise results.

Count every tracked part line
Write the counted quantity next to the expected one
Mark lines missing more than your tolerance
Hand the sheet to the office the same day
Office enters the count and checks the variance
Print the restock list
Order from your parts counter and your equipment supplier
Pick up the order and check it against the list
Load the van and tick each line
Enter the restock on the Restocks sheet
File the supplier invoice
Write each part used on the work order
Enter the parts on the Parts Used sheet
Mark parts taken from the van
Check that every part is billed
Chase any unbilled part with the office
Check the part is unused and in its pack
Write the return on the Parts Return Sheet
Take the part back to your parts counter
Ask for a credit note
Match the credit to the supplier invoice
Write the change on the Supplier Price Changes sheet
Check the Price Change Margin Impact tool
Update the price-book lines that fell under target
Check the open estimates
Tell the technicians about the new prices
Open the restock list on Monday
Add parts for the jobs booked this week
Send the order to your parts counter
Confirm the pick-up time
Check the delivery against the order
File the invoice and note the due date
Check fuel level and tyres on each van
Check the van papers are inside
Note any damage or noise
Log the week on the Vehicle Costs sheet
Book the garage
Plan which jobs move for the day
Tell the technician the date
Take the van in
Enter the cost on the Vehicle Costs sheet
Set the next service date
Enter fuel, repairs and tyres for each van
Check cost per working day against your budget
Compare each van with the shop average
Open the Keep Replace or Add a Van tool for the highest van
Note the decision in the owner meeting
Write the request with the cost and the life in years
Check the budget in the Tool Replacement Plan
Owner approves or waits
Buy the tool and keep the receipt
Enter it on the Tools and Equipment sheet
Assign it to a technician
Open the Tool Purchase Log tool
Check which tools are past their life

Recount the parts with the largest gaps
